result.abstract: This lecture describes the anatomy of the larynx: its situation and fixation, its nine cartilages, joints, ligaments, intrinsic and extrinsic muscles, compartments, histology, relations, blood supply, lymphatic drainage and innervation. It then explains the physiology of phonation and the acoustic parameters of the voice. It ends with clinical correlations: laryngeal nerve damage, laryngeal obstruction and vocal nodules.

concepts.name: Larynx
concepts.definition: The upper expanded part of the lower respiratory tract, modified for producing voice: an unpaired median tube of cartilages linked by joints, muscles and ligaments and lined by mucous membrane. It acts as a sphincter at the inlet of the lower respiratory tract.

evidence.quote: The larynx is the upper expanded part of the lower respiratory tract, modified for producing voice, also called the organ of phonation
It acts as a sphincter at the inlet of lower respiratory tract to protect the trachea and the bronchial tree

concepts.name: Thyroid cartilage
concepts.definition: Large unpaired laryngeal cartilage shaped like an open book, open backwards, with two vertical quadrilateral laminae, superior and inferior thyroid incisures and superior and inferior cornua; the inferior cornu carries a cricoid articular surface.

evidence.quote: Shaped like an open book, open backwards, with two vertical quadrilateral laminae
a thick vertical posterior margin extended by the superior and inferior cornua, the inferior carrying a cricoid articular surface

concepts.name: Cricoid cartilage
concepts.definition: Unpaired signet-shaped ring of cartilage with a narrow anterior arch and a broad posterior lamina, at the level of C6. It is the only cartilage that completely encircles the lumen of the larynx and is called the foundation stone of the larynx.

evidence.quote: A signet-shaped ring with a narrow anterior arch and a broad posterior lamina, at C6
The cricoid cartilage is situated at the level of C6 vertebra and completely encircles the lumen of the larynx

concepts.name: Epiglottis
concepts.definition: Large unpaired laryngeal cartilage shaped like a tennis racket. Its posterior (laryngeal) side faces the vestibule and its anterior (lingual) side the base of the tongue and hyoid; its base is superior and free and its foot inserts into the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage.

evidence.quote: Shaped like a tennis racket with a curved lower handle forming its foot
Shape: tennis racket with curved lower handle forming the foot of the epiglottis

concepts.name: Arytenoid cartilage
concepts.definition: Small paired laryngeal cartilage shaped like a triangular pyramid about 15 mm high. Its apex articulates with the corniculate cartilage and its concave base with the cricoid lamina; the base bears the vocal process anteriorly and the muscular process laterally.

evidence.quote: Triangular pyramids about 15 mm high. The apex articulates with the corniculate cartilage, the concave base with the cricoid lamina
The anterior angle of the base is extended by the vocal process

concepts.name: Corniculate cartilage
concepts.definition: Small paired accessory cartilage of the larynx lying on the apex of the arytenoid cartilage, with which it articulates.

evidence.quote: Corniculate: on the apices of the arytenoids
Three paired and small: arytenoid, corniculate, cuneiform

concepts.name: Cuneiform cartilage
concepts.definition: Small paired accessory cartilage of the larynx lying in the aryepiglottic fold.

evidence.quote: Cuneiform: in the aryepiglottic fold
Three paired and small: arytenoid, corniculate, cuneiform

concepts.name: Vocal process
concepts.definition: The extension of the anterior angle of the base of the arytenoid cartilage, which gives insertion to the vocal ligament.

evidence.quote: The anterior angle of the base extends as the vocal process (insertion of the vocal ligament)
The vocal process gives insertion to the : • Vocal ligament

concepts.name: Cricoarytenoid joint
concepts.definition: Elliptical synovial joint uniting the base of the arytenoid with the upper edge of the cricoid lamina, reinforced by the posterior cricoarytenoid ligament. Functionally the most important laryngeal joint, allowing rotation of the arytenoid around a vertical axis and gliding of the arytenoids toward or away from each other.

evidence.quote: An elliptical synovial articulation reinforced by the posterior cricoarytenoid ligament, uniting the base of the arytenoid with the upper edge of the cricoid lamina
Rotatory movement, in which arytenoid cartilage moves around a vertical axis, thus abducting or adducting the vocal cords

concepts.name: Cricothyroid joint
concepts.definition: Flat synovial joint, reinforced by ligaments, joining the lower cornu of the thyroid cartilage and the lateral face of the cricoid cartilage. It allows tilting of the cricoid around a transverse axis, the arch up and the lamina down.

evidence.quote: A flat synovial joint reinforced by ligaments, joining the lower cornu of the thyroid cartilage and the lateral face of the cricoid
Flat synovial joint reinforced by ligaments joining the lower cornu of the thyroid cartilage and the lateral face of the cricoid cartilage

concepts.name: Thyrohyoid membrane
concepts.definition: Extrinsic membrane of the larynx running from the upper edge of the thyroid cartilage to the lower edge of the hyoid bone, with a medial and two lateral thickenings. The internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve and the superior laryngeal artery perforate it.

evidence.quote: Thyrohyoid membrane: from the upper edge of the thyroid cartilage to the lower edge of the hyoid bone
Enters the larynx with the superior laryngeal artery by perforating the thyrohyoid membrane

concepts.name: Thyroepiglottic ligament
concepts.definition: Extrinsic ligament of the larynx attaching the lower narrow end (foot) of the epiglottis to the posterior surface of the thyroid angle.

evidence.quote: Thyroepiglottic ligament: attaches the lower narrow end of the epiglottis to the posterior surface of the thyroid angle
inferior inserts into the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage through the thyroepiglottic ligament

concepts.name: Cricothyroid ligament
concepts.definition: Intrinsic ligament of the larynx, part of the fibroelastic inner tube, described as stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process, where it forms the vocal ligament. With the cricoid it surrounds the infraglottic cavity.

evidence.quote: The cricothyroid ligament, stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process, forms the vocal ligament
The cavity below the vocal cords, surrounded by the cricoid and the cricothyroid ligament

concepts.name: Vocal ligament
concepts.definition: Ligament formed by the cricothyroid ligament between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process of the arytenoid, on which it inserts. Together with muscle it makes up the vocal cord.

evidence.quote: The cricothyroid ligament, stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process, forms the vocal ligament
The vocal process gives insertion to the : • Vocal ligament

concepts.name: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: Paired intrinsic muscle of the larynx inserting on the muscular process of the arytenoid. It is the only dilator of the glottis and the only intrinsic muscle that abducts the vocal cords, hence called the safety muscle of the larynx.

evidence.quote: Posterior cricoarytenoids are the only abductors: the safety muscles of the larynx
Posterior ericoarytenoids: abduct the vocal cords

concepts.name: Lateral cricoarytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: Paired intrinsic muscle of the larynx inserting on the muscular process of the arytenoid; a constrictor of the glottis that adducts the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: the lateral angle bears the muscular process (insertion of the posterior and lateral cricoarytenoid muscles)
Lateral cricoarytenoids: adduct the vocal cords

concepts.name: Transverse arytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: The only unpaired intrinsic muscle of the larynx, inserting on the posterior side of the arytenoid cartilages; a constrictor of the glottis that adducts the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: All the intrinsic muscles are paired except the transverse arytenoid (interarytenoid), which is unpaired
Posterior side: gives insertion to the transverse arytenoid muscle

concepts.name: Cricothyroid muscle
concepts.definition: Paired intrinsic muscle and the only one lying on the outer aspect of the larynx. It elevates the cricoid arch and lowers the thyroid cartilage, tensing the vocal cord, and is important for the tone and pitch of the voice.

evidence.quote: Vocal cord tensors: cricothyroid (paired). Action: elevation of the cricoid arch and lowering of the thyroid cartilage, tensing the vocal cord
Crivothyroid: tenses the vocal cords

concepts.name: Vocalis muscle
concepts.definition: Intrinsic muscle of the larynx, named in the lecture as the inferior thyroarytenoid, running from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid. It tilts the arytenoid forward and tenses the vocal cord.

evidence.quote: inferior thyroarytenoid or vocal muscle (from the reentrant angle to the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid), which tilts the arytenoid forward and tenses the cord
Vocals: tenses the vocal cords

concepts.name: Thyroarytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: Intrinsic muscle of the larynx that relaxes the vocal cords. The lecture lists a superior part, from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the lower third of the arytenoid, and an inferior part among the constrictors of the glottis.

evidence.quote: Relax the vocal cords | Thyroarytenoid
Thyroarytenoid: relaxes the vocal cords

concepts.name: Intrinsic laryngeal muscle
concepts.definition: Muscle of the larynx classified by its action as a vocal cord tensor, dilator of the glottis or constrictor of the glottis. All are paired except the transverse arytenoid, and all are supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve except the cricothyroid.

evidence.quote: All the intrinsic muscles are paired except the transverse arytenoid (interarytenoid), which is unpaired
Recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies all intrinsic muscles except the cricothyroid

concepts.name: Extrinsic laryngeal muscle
concepts.definition: Muscle ensuring laryngeal mobility, especially during swallowing. The elevators are the thyrohyoid, mylohyoid and digastric; the depressors are the sternothyroid, sternohyoid and omohyoid.

evidence.quote: Extrinsic muscles ensure laryngeal mobility, especially during swallowing. Elevators: thyrohyoid, mylohyoid, digastric. Depressors: sternothyroid, sternohyoid, omohyoid
Extrinsic muscles: ensure laryngeal mobility especially during swallowing

concepts.name: Vocal fold abduction
concepts.definition: Movement in which the arytenoids rotate so that their vocal processes move laterally, giving a wide diamond-shaped opening of the glottis that lets air through the rima glottidis.

evidence.quote: the muscular processes of both arytenoids rotate medially and the vocal processes rotate laterally, giving a wide diamond-shaped opening
moves around a vertical axis, thus abducting or adducting the vocal cords

concepts.name: Vocal fold adduction
concepts.definition: Movement bringing the vocal cords together, produced by rotation of the arytenoids around a vertical axis at the cricoarytenoid joint. Keeping the cords adducted is the first step of voice production.

evidence.quote: Rotatory movement around a vertical axis, abducting or adducting the vocal cords
The voice is produced in following manner: 1. Vocal cords are kept adducted

concepts.name: Vocal fold tension
concepts.definition: Tightening of the vocal cord that makes it ready to vibrate when sound is about to be produced; it is produced by tilting of the cricoid around a transverse axis at the cricothyroid joint.

evidence.quote: Tilting of the cricoid around a transverse axis (arch up, lamina down) tenses the vocal cords
when sound is about to be produced it tenses the cord and makes it ready to vibrate

concepts.name: Laryngeal vestibule
concepts.definition: Pyramidal space of the supraglottic compartment of the larynx, extending from the laryngeal margin to the ventricular bands: the space above the vestibular folds.

evidence.quote: Vestibule: a pyramidal space from the laryngeal margin to the ventricular bands
vestibule above the vestibular folds

concepts.name: Laryngeal ventricle
concepts.definition: Cavity of the supraglottic compartment of the larynx lying between the ventricular bands (false vocal cords, vestibular folds) above and the plane of the vocal cords below.

evidence.quote: Laryngeal or Morgagni ventricle: between the ventricular bands (false vocal cords) above and the plane of the vocal cords below
ventricle between them and the vocal folds

concepts.name: Glottis
concepts.definition: The compartment of the larynx at the level of the two vocal cords, which delimit a triangular opening. It is narrower than the vestibular cleft.

evidence.quote: The glottis is triangular and narrower than the vestibular cleft
Glottis: delimited by the 2 vocal cords, it is triangular in shape

concepts.name: Vocal fold
concepts.definition: One of two pearly white cords stretched between the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage in front and the arytenoid cartilage behind, made of vocal ligament and muscle. The two unite anteriorly at the anterior commissure and are separated posteriorly by the interarytenoid region.

evidence.quote: Two pearly white vocal cords stretched between the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage in front and the arytenoid behind, made of vocal ligament and muscle
2 pearly white cords stretched between the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage in front and the arytenoid cartilage in back

concepts.name: Infraglottic cavity
concepts.definition: The cavity of the larynx below the vocal cords, surrounded by the cricoid cartilage and the cricothyroid ligament.

evidence.quote: The cavity below the vocal cords, surrounded by the cricoid and the cricothyroid ligament
Infraglottic cavity — space inferior to vocal folds

concepts.name: Superior laryngeal artery
concepts.definition: Branch of the superior thyroid artery that enters the larynx through the thyrohyoid membrane with the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve. It supplies the supraglottic part and anastomoses with the posteroinferior laryngeal artery.

evidence.quote: Superior laryngeal artery | A branch of the superior thyroid artery. Supplies the supraglottic part and anastomoses with the posteroinferior laryngeal artery
branch of the Superior Thyroid Artery, it vascularizes the supraglottic part and anastomoses with ALPI

concepts.name: Posteroinferior laryngeal artery
concepts.definition: Branch of the inferior thyroid artery that supplies the posterior part of the laryngeal mucosa and anastomoses with the superior laryngeal artery.

evidence.quote: Posteroinferior laryngeal artery | A branch of the inferior thyroid artery. Supplies the posterior part of the laryngeal mucosa
branch of the Inferior Thyroid Artery. It vascularizes the posterior part of the laryngeal mucosa

concepts.name: Superior laryngeal nerve
concepts.definition: Branch of the vagus, mixed but essentially sensory, that descends against the pharyngeal wall and divides behind the greater horn of the hyoid into an internal and an external branch.

evidence.quote: A branch of the vagus, mixed but essentially sensory, descending against the pharyngeal wall and dividing behind the greater horn of the hyoid

concepts.name: Internal laryngeal nerve
aliases: internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
concepts.definition: Branch of the superior laryngeal nerve that enters the larynx with the superior laryngeal artery by perforating the thyrohyoid membrane. It gives sensory innervation to the mucosa above the vocal folds, plus autonomic fibres.

evidence.quote: Internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve: sensation above the cords, piercing the thyrohyoid membrane
Pierces thyrohyoid membrane + Sensory from mucosa above vocal folds

concepts.name: External laryngeal nerve
aliases: external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
concepts.definition: Branch of the superior laryngeal nerve that innervates the cricothyroid muscle. The lecture also says it perforates the cricothyroid membrane and gives sensory innervation to the subglottic stage.

evidence.quote: External branch | Innervates the cricothyroid muscle and perforates the cricothyroid membrane; sensory innervation of the subglottic stage
External branch - innervates cricothyroid m

concepts.name: Recurrent laryngeal nerve
concepts.definition: Branch of the vagus arising on the right at the base of the neck and on the left in the thorax. It is motor to all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except the cricothyroid and sensory below the vocal folds.

evidence.quote: From the vagus, on the right at the base of the neck and on the left at the thorax. Motor to all the intrinsic muscles except the cricothyroid
Recurrent laryngeal n. + Motor to intrinsic muscles of larynx

concepts.name: Lymphatic drainage of the larynx
concepts.definition: Laryngeal lymphatics are very rich in the supraglottic zone, thinner in the subglottic zone and absent at the vocal cords. The supraglottic region drains to the internal jugular chain; the infraglottic region to pretracheal and paratracheal nodes and the internal jugular chain.

evidence.quote: Very rich in the supraglottic zone, thinner in the subglottic zone, absent at the vocal cords. Supraglottic: the internal jugular chain
Very rich in the supraglottic zones, thinner in the subglottic zone, absent in the vocal cords

concepts.name: Laryngeal mucosa
concepts.definition: Thin, smooth, pale pink lining of the larynx, continuous with the pharyngeal mucosa above and the tracheal mucosa below. Its epithelium is respiratory type (cylindric stratified) except at the vocal cords and upper half of the epiglottis, where it is non-keratinized stratified squamous.

evidence.quote: The epithelium is respiratory type (cylindric stratified) throughout, except at the vocal cords and the upper half of the epiglottis, which are non-keratinized stratified squamous
Thin, smooth, pale pink in color. It continues above with the pharyngeal mucosa and below with the tracheal mucosa

concepts.name: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury
concepts.definition: Damage to the recurrent laryngeal nerve, often accidental during partial thyroidectomy. Unilaterally, the cord on the affected side lies in the paramedian position and does not vibrate, though the other usually compensates; bilaterally, both cords lie paramedian with loss of phonation and difficulty breathing.

evidence.quote: Recurrent laryngeal nerve, often damaged accidentally during partial thyroidectomy: unilaterally, the cord lies in the paramedian position and does not vibrate, though the other usually compensates
Unilateral recurrent nerve palsy: paramedian cord

concepts.name: Cadaveric position of the vocal cords
concepts.definition: Position in which the vocal cords are further abducted and fixed because all the intrinsic muscles are paralysed, seen when both the recurrent and the external laryngeal nerves are damaged on both sides.

evidence.quote: If both recurrent and external laryngeal nerves are damaged on both sides, all the intrinsic muscles are paralysed and the cords are further abducted and fixed: the cadaveric position
This is known as the cadaveric postion of vocal cords

concepts.name: Vocal nodule
concepts.definition: Inflammatory nodule that develops in people who overuse the voice, at the junction of the anterior one third and posterior two thirds of the vocal cords, the area of maximum contact during vibration. Nodules are bilateral and symmetrical, soft and reddish early, later greyish or whitish.

evidence.quote: Vocal nodules form at the junction of the anterior third and posterior two thirds of the cords
teachers, pop singers, the inflammatory nodules develop at these sites called vocal nodules

concepts.name: Acoustic parameters of the voice
concepts.definition: The three parameters the lecture uses to characterise the voice: frequency, in Hertz, depending on the vibration speed of the vocal folds; intensity, in dB, depending on the force of pulmonary expiration; and pitch, depending on vocal fold accommodation and especially the shape of the supralaryngeal cavities.

evidence.quote: The voice is characterised by three acoustic parameters: frequency, in Hertz, depending on the vibration speed of the vocal folds
The voice is characterized by 3 acoustic parameters

concepts.name: Phonation
concepts.definition: The set of mechanisms allowing vibration at the free edge of the vocal fold, transforming aerodynamic energy into acoustic energy. The sound produced is then modified and filtered by the supralaryngeal air cavities to become vowels and consonants.

evidence.quote: The set of mechanisms allowing vibration at the free edge of the vocal fold, transforming aerodynamic energy into acoustic energy
The phonation (speech) is produced by the vibrations of the vocal cords

concepts.name: Vibratory cycle
concepts.definition: The cycle of vocal fold movement during phonation: the folds close as the arytenoids come together; they open when subglottic pressure overcomes the muscular and elastic resistance, letting a puff of air pass at high speed; then the folds close again.

evidence.quote: Putting into phonatory position: the folds close as the arytenoids come together
Opening: when the subglottic pressure overcomes the muscular and elastic resistance, a puff of air passes at high speed, an acoustic impulse

concepts.name: Supralaryngeal cavity
concepts.definition: One of the air cavities above the larynx, chiefly the pharynx and the oral cavity, which filter the laryngeal sound by resonance and shape it by articulation through the tongue, pharyngolarynx, jaws, lips and soft palate.

evidence.quote: The sound produced is immediately modified and filtered by the supralaryngeal air cavities to become vowels and consonants
Filter role: resonance and enrichment of certain frequencies or suppression of others, with two areas of particular enhancement, the pharynx and the oral cavity

concepts.name: Laryngeal obstruction
concepts.definition: Blockage of the larynx by a foreign body, causing choking when the explosive cough reflex set off by the very sensitive mucosa of the superior larynx is slowed or absent. The Heimlich manoeuvre of upward and backward abdominal thrusts is used to dislodge the foreign body.

evidence.quote: The mucosa of the superior larynx is very sensitive, so a foreign body causes immediate explosive coughing. If that reflex is slowed or absent, choking follows
give three or four abdominal thrusts directed upwards and backwards, squeezing the residual air up to dislodge the foreign body

concepts.name: Hyoid bone
concepts.definition: Bone lying above the larynx with the base of the tongue. The larynx is united to it through muscles and ligaments, and the thyrohyoid membrane reaches its lower edge.

evidence.quote: Above: the hyoid bone and base of the tongue
Top: hyoid bone and base of tongue

concepts.name: Trachea
concepts.definition: The airway lying below the larynx, with which the larynx is continuous. The cricotracheal ligament runs between the lower edge of the cricoid and the upper edge of the first tracheal ring.

evidence.quote: Above: the hyoid bone and base of the tongue. Below: the trachea
Cricotracheal ligament: between the lower edge of the cricoid and the upper edge of the first tracheal ring

concepts.name: Laryngeal prominence
concepts.definition: The forward bulge formed where the two laminae of the thyroid cartilage meet in the midline.

evidence.quote: The laryngeal prominence, the Adam's apple, formed where the two laminae of the thyroid cartilage meet in the midline
the forward bulge where the two thyroid laminae meet

concepts.name: External laryngeal nerve injury
concepts.definition: Lesion of the external laryngeal nerve that paralyses the cricothyroid muscle, giving weakness of phonation from loss of its tightening effect on the vocal cords. The voice change is especially noticeable in singers.

evidence.quote: External laryngeal nerve: weakness of phonation from loss of the tightening effect of the cricothyroid
Paralysis after an external laryngeal nerve lesion alters the voice significantly, especially noticeable in singers

More than 50 things met the selection rules. Left out because of the limit, and mentioned inside other definitions where possible: anteroinferior laryngeal artery, Heimlich manoeuvre, cricotracheal ligament, hyoepiglottic ligament, vestibular ligament, vestibular fold (false vocal cord), muscular process of the arytenoid, superior and inferior thyroid arteries, vagus nerve.

Slide 37 and slide 64 are badly garbled by OCR (two-column textbook page); quotes from them are copied as they appear, including misspellings such as 'ericoarytenoids', 'Crivothyroid', 'Vocals' and 'postion'.

Vocalis and thyroarytenoid: the packet lists them separately in its action table (vocalis tenses, thyroarytenoid relaxes) but also names the inferior thyroarytenoid as the vocal muscle. I kept two concepts and linked them with related-to rather than part-of.

Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury: the summary and card say phonation is not much affected in unilateral damage because the other cord compensates, while hy:6 gives 'hoarse voice' for unilateral palsy and 'stridor, airway emergency' for bilateral. I did not treat this as a contradiction; the definition follows the summary section.

The cricothyroid ligament is described in the summary as stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process, and in card g6 as lying between the cricoid and thyroid cartilages; the packet also calls it the cricothyroid membrane (deeper:3). Treated as one concept with medium confidence.
Glottis and rima glottidis are treated as one concept because the packet's question on the rima glottidis is explained with the description of the glottis.

findings.detail: The definition makes the superior and inferior thyroarytenoid 'parts' of the one thyroarytenoid muscle that relaxes the cords. The packet lists them as two separate constrictors and never says they are parts of the 'Thyroarytenoid' of the action table; the inferior one is the vocal muscle, which the packet says tenses the cord (and which the result itself gives as an alias of the vocalis concept). Neither evidence quote states the parts.

findings.detail: 'Rima glottidis' is the standard name of a different, narrower thing: the opening between the vocal cords, which is how the packet's own question defines it. The concept is defined as the compartment at the level of the vocal cords, and the result makes the vocal fold part-of it, so it is not the gap. The packet's loose use should have gone under conflicts, not aliases.

findings.detail: The definition says the cricothyroid ligament is stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process. Standard teaching: the cricothyroid ligament (conus elasticus) rises from the upper border of the cricoid; only its free upper margin, between the thyroid angle and the vocal process, is the vocal ligament, and its median part joins cricoid arch to thyroid cartilage. The packet itself gives the cricoid-to-thyroid version elsewhere. The result mentions this only in notes; it is not under conflicts, so nothing is listed in affects.
